claims.text: In the space of just three weeks, the UN Human Rights Office documented 15 drone strikes on El Obeid, which killed at least 45 civilians. El Obeid has more than half a million residents, together with at least 100,000 internally displaced persons, and the number of newly displaced people across Kordofan has risen by nearly two-thirds in only three months.

Re-checked 3 August 2026: a search of reliefweb.int and news.un.org found no new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond those already cited; siege and drone-strike conditions continue with no ceasefire or ground assault reported.

G7 Foreign Ministers' joint statement on El Obeid, Sudan (14 July 2026): condemns ongoing RSF drone strikes on El Obeid and obstruction of humanitarian access, references the precedent of atrocities in El Fasher, and calls for an immediate ceasefire and compliance with the Jeddah Declaration to protect civilians.

NRC report (posted 7 July 2026) on El Obeid: families are dying from drone strikes and from hunger as the siege continues, with an aid convoy struck the preceding week; essential services and food access are collapsing further as the blockade persists.

UN News (17 July 2026): the UN human rights chief warned that civilians in El Obeid "have been under siege for 18 months" and face continuous drone strikes, with more than 100,000 displaced people sheltering in camps in the city. WFP is providing food assistance to over 100,000 people in those camps, including nutrition support for 17,000 children, but is distributing only a reduced ration that recipients are sharing with other families. Almost 20 million people in Sudan are now classified as acutely food insecure, and more than 14 million people have been uprooted nationwide since the conflict began.

WFP Geneva Palais briefing note (published 17 July 2026): El Obeid city (population approximately 500,000) is hosting displaced people, with more than 120,000 people in the 'Unified IDP Camp' alone. WFP is providing food/cash assistance to just over 100,000 people in camps inside the city, but severe funding shortfalls mean recipients are only receiving 50 percent of the ration they should. Fuel scarcity has crippled partner logistics, forcing WFP to deploy its own fleet vehicles to keep distributions running.

UNFPA Flash Update #2 on the situation in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan (published 20 July 2026, covering 1-19 July): 21 drone-related incidents were recorded in and around El Obeid between 1-19 July 2026, causing civilian casualties (no aggregate death toll given), damage to critical infrastructure, and further disruption to already-limited essential services, with severe constraints on sexual and reproductive health and gender-based-violence response services due to insecurity and resource shortages.

UN News (24 July 2026), citing a UN Women statement: 'More than half a million people live [in El Obeid], including 83,000 internally displaced people, most of them women and children.' Drone strikes have targeted water points and distribution sites during the day, forcing women and girls to wait until nightfall to collect water, where they face sexual violence instead — UN Women describes this as leaving 'no safe window' to access water. Nationwide, 'drone strikes killed at least 880 civilians in the first four months of 2026 alone — more than 80 per cent of all civilian deaths recorded by the human rights office in that period.' The number of women and girls needing gender-based-violence services nationwide has quadrupled since the conflict began, reaching an estimated 12.7 million in 2026, and cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: no allowlisted source has published a new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count (45+ killed) and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure (120,000+); siege and drone-strike conditions continue with no de-escalation, ceasefire, or ground assault reported.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: UNHCR's Sudan Situation Monthly External Update #120 (June 2026, posted 31 July 2026) notes continued drone attacks on El Obeid damaging civilian areas, fuel infrastructure, health facilities and transport routes, but reports no new aggregate casualty or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond the sources already cited; siege conditions continue with no ceasefire or ground assault confirmed.

description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary forces have besieged El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state, subjecting the city of more than half a million residents to relentless drone strikes and blockade conditions. As of 24 July 2026, the siege continues with no ceasefire and no ground assault yet confirmed by authoritative sources. Drone strikes have intensified (21 incidents recorded 1-19 July per a UNFPA Flash Update on ReliefWeb, up from 15 strikes over three weeks in the prior UN Human Rights Office count) and the humanitarian situation remains dire: WFP reported more than 120,000 people sheltering in the city's Unified IDP Camp alone (17 July briefing), with food rations cut to 50 percent of full entitlement due to funding shortfalls, while a separate UN News/UN Women report (24 July 2026) put El Obeid's IDP population at 83,000 out of a total city population of more than half a million — a lower figure than the WFP camp count, likely reflecting a different counting methodology or reference date, and not treated here as superseding the more specific WFP camp figure. That 24 July report also describes a 'dual terror' facing women and girls, who face drone strikes if they collect water by day and sexual violence if they wait until night, and cites a nationwide (not El Obeid-specific) figure that drone strikes killed at least 880 civilians across Sudan in the first four months of 2026 alone — more than 80 percent of all civilian deaths recorded by the UN human rights office in that period — plus a UN Women estimate that 12.7 million women and girls nationwide now need gender-based-violence services, having quadrupled since the conflict began. No updated aggregate civilian death toll specific to El Obeid has been issued since the UN's 3 July report of at least 45 killed. G7 foreign ministers condemned the siege on 14 July 2026, and UN officials continue to warn of the risk of large-scale atrocities similar to those already documented in El Fasher, Darfur.

impact.summary: No updated aggregate death toll specific to El Obeid has been published since the 3 July UN Human Rights Office figure (15 drone strikes over 3 weeks, at least 45 civilians killed); drone strikes have continued and even increased in frequency (21 drone-related incidents logged 1-19 July per a UNFPA Flash Update via ReliefWeb), but no authoritative source has issued a new cumulative city-specific casualty count as of 24 July 2026. A UN News article citing UN Women (24 July 2026) reports a nationwide figure that drone strikes killed at least 880 civilians across Sudan in the first four months of 2026 alone (over 80% of all civilian deaths the UN human rights office recorded in that period) — this is a national, not El-Obeid-specific, statistic and is presented as additional context rather than a revision of the city death toll. On displacement, WFP (17 July briefing) confirms more than 120,000 people are in the Unified IDP Camp alone in El Obeid, the most specific and best-corroborated camp-population figure to date; a separate 24 July UN News/UN Women report cites a lower total of 83,000 IDPs in El Obeid (out of a city population of over half a million), which is noted here as a divergent source figure rather than adopted as the headline number. Rations for WFP-assisted families remain cut to 50 percent of the full entitlement due to funding shortfalls. The 24 July report also documents that women and girls face drone strikes if they collect water by day and sexual violence if they wait until after dark, with no safe window to access water. No ceasefire, siege-lifting, or ground assault has been confirmed by an authoritative source. Re-checked 3 August 2026: no allowlisted source has published a new aggregate death toll or IDP figure specific to El Obeid beyond those already cited (the 3 July UN Human Rights Office count of 45+ killed and the 17 July WFP camp-population figure of 120,000+); siege and drone-strike conditions continue with no ceasefire or ground assault reported.

event.scale: City under siege; UN human-rights atrocity-risk warning

name: Siege of El Obeid — North Kordofan, Sudan
